svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-insurance-vs-ltr-str-revenue; chapter number: 2; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: Insurance Housing Against Long-Term and Short-Term Rent; subtitle: Metro Atlanta case studies and a Smyrna Coverage D budget; caption: Reported monthly figures for the same markets across long-term, short-term, and insurance midterm models, plus a worked Coverage D budget.; assumptions note: Typical values are the figures the speakers stated, not computed midpoints. The Smyrna budget strips roughly 10% land value from a $480K purchase using a cost segregation study.; note: Ruben Kanya's Atlanta 4-bedroom figures via Rich Somers (g075AOuQIwk) and Smyrna math via Landlord Diaries - The Monthly Rentals Podcast (vbHlGVZKjvg); Anya Sher's 3/2 via Real Estate Pros Show (-OpbvAckfkQ).; unit: USD per month; bars: label: Atlanta 4BR long-term rent; min: 2000; max: 2200; typical: 2000; display: $2,000-2,200; label: Atlanta 4BR short-term revenue; min: 5000; max: 7000; typical: 5000; display: $5K average, $7K peak; label: Atlanta 4BR insurance midterm; min: 7950; max: 7950; typical: 7950; display: $7,950 average at 100% occupancy; label: Metro Atlanta 3/2, long-term to insurance; min: 2000; max: 6300; typical: 6300; display: ~$2,000 LTR, ~$4,500 STR, $6,300 insurance; label: Smyrna Coverage D monthly budget; min: 7200; max: 14400; typical: 7200; display: $7,200 over 12 months, $14,400 over 6
